neighbors.establishing_passage: Generated inpainted images with erased fovea and retinal vessels separately; sex-prediction AUC was 0.881 (0.877-0.885) in the fovea-erased image and 0.682 (0.676-0.688) in the retinal-vessel-erased image versus the original model, indicating retinal vessels are important features for deep learning sex prediction.

Males have richer retinal vasculature networks with a higher number of branches and nodes and a larger total length of branches in the vessel graph; vessels cover a greater area in the superior temporal quadrant in males vs females.

Crossref metadata confirms title 'Quantifying regional contributions to sex classification from fundus photographs via a two-stage attention-based deep learning approach', authors Joseph Kim and Shina Jang, Scientific Reports, published 2026-05-20; attention-based region weighting, not a branch-selective causal intervention.

neighbors.identifier: DOI 10.1038/s41586-026-10181-8, PMID 41781626 (Blankemeier et al., Merlin, Nature 2026; arXiv 2406.06512)
neighbors.establishing_passage: Applies the latent-shift counterfactual method to investigate image features used for classification; the size of the spleen is reduced in the counterfactual relative to the original image (splenomegaly example). No input-space liver/spleen HU perturbation described; weights publicly released (GitHub/HF StanfordMIMI, MIT license).

neighbors.identifier: arXiv:2607.20993 (Sparse Concept Channels in Frozen 3D CT Vision Encoders, 2026)
neighbors.establishing_passage: Turning off the channels tied to one finding, that finding's score collapses while unrelated labels stay stable; the same sparse probe replicates on an architecturally unrelated 3D abdominal VLM (Merlin). Representation-space only; no input-space organ-HU perturbation, no steatosis/liver-spleen question.

Contrast-enhanced volumetric hepatosplenic attenuation derived using a fully automated deep learning CT tool for categoric steatosis assessment; indicators include the liver-spleen attenuation ratio, liver-spleen attenuation difference, and liver attenuation thresholding — the spleen reference is engineered in, not emergent.

The histologically proved reference range of hepatic attenuation minus splenic attenuation values for nonsteatotic livers was 1-18 HU (biopsy-proven donors, nonenhanced CT). Anchor verified as correctly cited by the card.

RoentMod generates realistic CXRs with user-specified synthetic pathology while preserving other anatomical features; state-of-the-art multi-task and foundation models frequently exploit off-target pathology as shortcuts, evaluated by paired classifier response to edits. Edits pathology, not a named vessel.

Intervenes on the size of anatomical structures including left lung area, right lung area, and heart area with locally coherent counterfactual edits on PadChest; graded structure-specific editing, never applied to the azygos vein or vascular pedicle.

AI software automatically delineates each cardiovascular border when a CXR is inputted, with width calculated by measuring distance from the midline; covers cardiovascular/great-vessel borders but does not isolate an azygos-arch localizer.

Width of azygos vein related to central venous pressure: strong (logarithmic, r~0.8) correlation between azygos width on chest radiograph and right atrial/central venous pressure. Pinned as the card's requested primary quantitative azygos-congestion citation.

nnU-Net pleural-effusion segmentation plus random-forest simple-vs-complex classification; radiomic shape features (elongation, flatness, sphericity, surface area) were largely NOT selected during training — density/HU features proved more informative; external validation on NLST and PleThora, not CT-RATE. NOTE: the card's PMID 35923880 is a plant circadian-clock paper and the author is Sexauer, not 'Ebert'; the card's PMCID was correct.

neighbors.identifier: arXiv:2502.07156 (Explaining 3D Computed Tomography Classifiers with Counterfactuals, 2025)
neighbors.establishing_passage: Adapts latent-shift counterfactual generation via a VQ-GAN autoencoder to 3D chest-CT classifiers; for pleural effusion the counterfactuals reveal reduced fluid accumulation around the lungs — fluid amount itself changes; volume is not preserved and interface curvature is not manipulated.

neighbors.identifier: arXiv:2608.11422 (COGENT: Counterfactual Gaussian Explanations for Volumetric Medical Images)
neighbors.establishing_passage: Counterfactual explanations in the parameter space of 3D Gaussian volumetric representations, optimized via differentiable rendering with gradients from a frozen downstream predictor (Sybil); general volumetric probing, no fluid-shape or fixed-volume interface-geometry control.

CT postprocessing defines the double-oblique plane of the esophageal hiatus, on which the hiatal surface area is manually traced; subjects with hernia had larger mean hiatus areas than matched controls (6.9 vs 2.5 cm2, p<0.0001). Pinned as the primary quantitative hiatus-measurement citation.

Crural length and intercrural distance are used to calculate hiatal surface area; an HSA of >=3.5 cm2 as the diagnostic cut-off gave 94.6% preoperative sensitivity for hiatal hernia; measurement remained a manual radiologist MPR tracing (ICC 1.00 radiologist vs surgeon).

neighbors.identifier: arXiv:2604.24146 (EXACT: an explainable anomaly-aware vision foundation model, 2026)
neighbors.establishing_passage: CT-CLIP degraded to an AUROC of 0.66 for hiatal hernia on RAD-ChestCT; cross-modal alignment objectives are not designed to preserve the fine-grained spatial structure required for precise localization of focal pathologies such as hiatal hernias. Benchmark/XAI only; no anatomical attribution to crural aperture vs sac volume.
